title: Testicular Cancer (germ cell)
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) in our own words - the physician decides. Full germ-cell pathway: workup -> histology / disease state -> stage and IGCCCG risk stratification -> stage/subtype/marker-directed FIRST-LINE arms -> RESPONSE-ADAPTED restaging after chemotherapy (complete response vs residual mass vs rising markers) -> residual-mass surgery with post-resection-histology-directed adjuvant -> surveillance -> relapse pathway with LINE-OF-THERAPY salvage (platinum-sensitive conventional-dose, refractory high-dose + ASCT, later-line) . Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; modalities without a dose protocol (surveillance, radiotherapy, RPLND, high-dose chemo/ASCT) are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup, staging, risk, response, and surveillance content is standard oncology in our own words; no proprietary guideline text reproduced. Invents no dose/regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison), Testicular Cancer. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols and their own evidence layers; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Serum tumour markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) must be drawn before orchiectomy and again after, with post-orchiectomy decline tracked against expected half-lives (AFP ~5-7 days, hCG ~1-3 days). A raised AFP is incompatible with pure seminoma and mandates NSGCT management.

b.text: IGCCCG risk group is assigned only for metastatic (stage II-III) disease and uses primary site, non-pulmonary visceral metastases, and post-orchiectomy marker levels. Pure seminoma is never classified as poor risk.

c.text: Sperm banking should be offered before orchiectomy or any gonadotoxic therapy. Discuss contralateral testis biopsy only in selected high-risk cases (atrophy, cryptorchidism, marked microlithiasis).

d.text: After first-line chemotherapy, re-image and repeat markers. Rising markers signal active disease and route to salvage systemic therapy, not surgery; normalised markers with a residual mass route to resection (post-chemotherapy RPLND in NSGCT; PET-directed observation vs biopsy/resection in seminoma).

e.text: Histology of the resected post-chemotherapy residual mass directs further therapy: necrosis/fibrosis needs no more treatment; mature teratoma is cured by complete resection alone; viable germ-cell tumour with adverse features may prompt two cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup after radical orchiectomy
nodes.description: Confirm germ-cell histology and establish stage before any systemic decision.

bullets.label: Radical inguinal orchiectomy for diagnosis and local control
bullets.sub: trans-scrotal biopsy is avoided (alters lymphatic drainage)

bullets.label: Serum tumour markers before AND after orchiectomy
bullets.sub: AFP, beta-hCG, LDH; track post-orchiectomy decline by half-life

bullets.label: Histology: seminoma vs non-seminomatous germ-cell tumour (NSGCT)
bullets.sub: any AFP elevation is treated as NSGCT regardless of histology

bullets.label: Brain MRI if poor-risk, high beta-hCG, or extensive lung metastases
Fertility counselling and sperm banking; assess gonadal function

bullets: Baseline audiometry and renal function before cisplatin

tables.title: Serum tumour markers in germ-cell tumours
rows: Elevation excludes pure seminoma; always NSGCT
May be modestly raised in seminoma or NSGCT
Non-specific; part of IGCCCG risk score

nodes.name: Histology / state
nodes.title: Histology and disease state
nodes.description: The seminoma vs NSGCT split, plus prior-chemo relapse, sets the whole pathway.

nodes.name: Seminoma stage
nodes.title: Seminoma: clinical stage
nodes.description: Stage drives whether adjuvant, definitive systemic, or observation applies.

tables.title: Seminoma stage groups (simplified)
rows: Surveillance preferred; adjuvant carbo or RT optional

nodes.name: Stage I seminoma option
nodes.title: Stage I seminoma: management choice
nodes.description: After orchiectomy most stage I seminoma is cured; choose the monitoring vs adjuvant trade-off.
bullets: Relapse risk untreated is roughly 15-20%, almost all salvaged at relapse
Adjuvant single-agent carboplatin or para-aortic RT each cut relapse to ~4%
Weigh late second-malignancy / cardiovascular risk of adjuvant therapy against surveillance imaging burden

nodes.name: Stage I seminoma surveillance
nodes.title: Stage I seminoma: active surveillance
nodes.description: No adjuvant therapy; structured imaging and marker follow-up, then routine surveillance.
bullets: Markers and clinical review at set intervals; cross-sectional abdomen/pelvis imaging over ~5 years
Chest imaging as indicated by symptoms or nodal findings
Treat relapse (usually retroperitoneal) with stage-directed chemotherapy or RT
Preferred for compliant patients wishing to avoid adjuvant toxicity

nodes.name: Stage I seminoma carboplatin
nodes.title: Stage I seminoma: adjuvant carboplatin
nodes.description: Single-agent carboplatin (AUC-based), typically one cycle, to lower relapse, then surveillance.
bullets: One cycle of AUC-dosed carboplatin; convenient, low acute toxicity
Reduces relapse versus surveillance without the RT late-effect profile
Enter routine post-treatment surveillance

nodes.name: Stage I seminoma RT
nodes.title: Stage I seminoma: adjuvant radiotherapy
nodes.description: Para-aortic (or dog-leg) radiotherapy; no dose protocol here - guidance only, then surveillance.
bullets: Low-dose para-aortic strip radiotherapy is highly effective at relapse control
Now used less than carboplatin/surveillance because of late second-cancer and cardiovascular risk
Radiotherapy is planned and delivered by radiation oncology - no systemic dose protocol
Enter routine post-treatment surveillance

nodes.name: Stage IIA/B seminoma choice
nodes.title: Stage IIA / IIB seminoma: RT vs chemotherapy
nodes.description: Node-limited seminoma; select radiotherapy for non-bulky nodes or cisplatin-based chemotherapy for bulkier disease.
bullets: Retroperitoneal RT is a long-standing option for non-bulky (IIA, small IIB) nodes
Cisplatin-based chemotherapy (EP x4 or BEP x3) is preferred for bulkier IIB and reduces in-field relapse
Chemotherapy routes into response-adapted restaging; RT routes to surveillance

nodes.name: Stage IIA/B seminoma RT
nodes.title: Stage IIA / IIB seminoma: retroperitoneal radiotherapy
nodes.description: Radiotherapy to involved retroperitoneal nodes for non-bulky stage II seminoma, then surveillance.
bullets: Modified dog-leg / para-aortic field covering the involved nodes for IIA and small IIB
High local control; chemotherapy is preferred as nodal bulk increases
Radiotherapy is delivered by radiation oncology - no systemic dose protocol
Enter routine post-treatment surveillance

nodes.name: Stage IIA/B seminoma chemotherapy
nodes.title: Stage IIA / IIB seminoma: BEP x3 or EP x4
nodes.description: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy for node-limited seminoma, then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: BEP x3 or EP x4 as for good-risk metastatic seminoma; preferred for bulkier IIB
Lower in-field relapse than RT for larger nodes
Reassess markers and imaging afterward on the restaging step
Backbones referenced below

nodes.name: Advanced seminoma risk
nodes.title: Advanced seminoma: IGCCCG risk
nodes.description: Stage IIC/III seminoma is good or intermediate risk only; poor risk does not exist for seminoma.

bullets.label: Good risk
bullets.sub: any primary site, any marker level, NO non-pulmonary visceral metastases

bullets.label: Intermediate risk
bullets.sub: presence of non-pulmonary visceral metastases (e.g. liver, bone, brain)

nodes.name: Good-risk seminoma
nodes.title: Good-risk advanced seminoma: BEP x3 or EP x4
nodes.description: Standard first-line cisplatin-based chemotherapy for good-risk seminoma, then restaging.
bullets: BEP x3 or EP x4 (EP avoids bleomycin lung toxicity in suitable patients)
Do not dose-reduce or delay without cause; dose intensity drives cure
Reassess with markers and imaging on the restaging step
Backbone regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Intermediate-risk seminoma
nodes.title: Intermediate-risk advanced seminoma: BEP x4
nodes.description: Intensified first-line chemotherapy for intermediate-risk seminoma, then restaging.
bullets: BEP x4 is standard; VIP x4 is an alternative if bleomycin is contraindicated
Reassess with markers and imaging on the restaging step
BEP backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Seminoma restaging
nodes.title: Seminoma: response-adapted restaging after chemotherapy
nodes.description: Re-image and repeat markers after first-line chemotherapy; the response pattern chooses the next step.
bullets: Complete response (markers normal, no residual mass): move to surveillance
Residual mass with normalised markers: size and FDG-PET decide observation vs intervention
Rising / plateaued markers: active disease - go to the relapse / salvage pathway

nodes.name: Seminoma residual mass
nodes.title: Seminoma: residual mass characterisation
nodes.description: Residual seminoma masses are usually fibrosis; FDG-PET (>= 6 weeks post-chemo) selects the few needing intervention.
bullets: Confirm markers have normalised first (rising markers = active disease, go to salvage)
Masses < 3 cm: observe without PET
Masses >= 3 cm: FDG-PET to distinguish viable tumour from necrosis

nodes.name: Seminoma residual observe
nodes.title: Seminoma residual (PET-negative): observation
nodes.description: PET-negative or small residual masses are observed, not resected, then routine surveillance.
bullets: Serial imaging and markers; most residual masses are fibrosis/necrosis and regress or stay stable
Resection is difficult (desmoplastic reaction) and reserved for growth or PET positivity
Enter routine post-treatment surveillance

nodes.name: Seminoma residual viable
nodes.title: Seminoma residual (PET-positive): biopsy / resection / salvage
nodes.description: PET-positive residual suggests viable tumour and needs tissue confirmation or systemic salvage.
bullets: Confirm with biopsy or resection where feasible (surgery is technically demanding)
Viable seminoma after first-line chemo is treated on the relapse / salvage pathway
Discuss at a multidisciplinary germ-cell tumour board

nodes.name: NSGCT stage
nodes.title: NSGCT: clinical stage
nodes.description: Stage and marker status route NSGCT to surveillance, primary RPLND, or chemotherapy.

tables.title: NSGCT stage groups (simplified)
rows: Risk-adapted surveillance vs BEP x1 vs RPLND
Marker status decides RPLND vs chemotherapy
Nodes > 5 cm or distant / persistently raised markers

nodes.name: Stage I NSGCT risk
nodes.title: Stage I NSGCT: relapse risk (LVI)
nodes.description: Lymphovascular invasion is the key predictor and separates low- from high-risk stage I NSGCT.

bullets.label: High risk
bullets.sub: lymphovascular invasion present (+/- high embryonal %); relapse ~40-50%

bullets: Markers must have normalised after orchiectomy to qualify as stage I

nodes.name: Stage I NSGCT low risk
nodes.title: Stage I NSGCT (low risk): surveillance preferred
nodes.description: No LVI - surveillance is preferred, with primary RPLND or one BEP as alternatives, then surveillance.
bullets: Active surveillance is preferred; most patients are cured by orchiectomy alone
Structured markers + imaging; relapse is treated with full first-line chemotherapy
Alternatives: one cycle of adjuvant BEP, or nerve-sparing primary RPLND
BEP backbone referenced below (used only if the adjuvant-chemo route is chosen)

nodes.name: Stage I NSGCT high risk
nodes.title: Stage I NSGCT (high risk): one cycle BEP or surveillance
nodes.description: LVI present - adjuvant BEP x1 markedly lowers relapse; surveillance or RPLND remain options, then surveillance.
bullets: One cycle of adjuvant BEP cuts relapse to roughly 3% and is a common choice
Surveillance remains valid for compliant patients accepting higher relapse risk
Nerve-sparing primary RPLND is an alternative, especially where chemo is undesirable
BEP backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Stage IIA/B NSGCT markers
nodes.title: Stage IIA / IIB NSGCT: marker status
nodes.description: Post-orchiectomy marker status decides whether primary RPLND or chemotherapy leads.
bullets: Persistently elevated markers indicate systemic disease - chemotherapy first
Normal markers with limited nodes allow a primary-RPLND route

nodes.name: Stage IIA/B NSGCT markers negative
nodes.title: Stage IIA / IIB NSGCT (markers normal): RPLND or chemotherapy
nodes.description: Marker-negative node-limited NSGCT can go to primary RPLND or BEP/EP, then restaging.
bullets: Nerve-sparing primary RPLND, with adjuvant chemo if pN+ with high nodal burden
Or primary cisplatin-based chemotherapy (BEP x3 / EP x4) then response-adapted restaging
Teratoma elements respond poorly to chemo and favour a surgical route
Chemotherapy backbones referenced below; RPLND is a surgical option

nodes.name: Stage IIA/B NSGCT markers positive
nodes.title: Stage IIA / IIB NSGCT (markers elevated): chemotherapy
nodes.description: Persistently raised markers mean systemic disease - treat with first-line chemotherapy, then restaging.
bullets: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy (BEP x3 or EP x4) as for good-risk metastatic disease
Manage any residual mass afterwards on the response-adapted restaging pathway
Backbones referenced below

nodes.name: Advanced NSGCT risk
nodes.title: Advanced NSGCT: IGCCCG risk group
nodes.description: Metastatic NSGCT is stratified good / intermediate / poor by primary site, visceral spread, and marker levels.

tables.title: IGCCCG risk for NSGCT
rows: Testis/retroperitoneal primary, no non-pulmonary visceral mets
As good but any single higher marker
Mediastinal primary OR non-pulmonary visceral mets
AFP > 10000, or hCG > 50000, or LDH > 10x ULN (any)

nodes.name: Good-risk NSGCT
nodes.title: Good-risk NSGCT: BEP x3 or EP x4
nodes.description: Standard first-line chemotherapy for good-risk metastatic NSGCT, then response-adapted restaging.
bullets: BEP x3, or EP x4 when bleomycin is best avoided (lung disease, older age, smoker)
Do not dose-reduce or delay without cause; dose intensity drives cure
Reassess markers and imaging on the restaging step
Backbones referenced below

nodes.name: Intermediate-risk NSGCT
nodes.title: Intermediate-risk NSGCT: BEP x4
nodes.description: Four cycles of BEP for intermediate-risk metastatic NSGCT, then restaging.
bullets: BEP x4 is standard; VIP x4 if bleomycin is contraindicated
Consider a marker-decline check to identify unfavourable kinetics
Reassess markers and imaging on the restaging step
BEP backbone referenced below

nodes.name: Poor-risk NSGCT
nodes.title: Poor-risk NSGCT: BEP x4 (or VIP x4)
nodes.description: Four cycles of BEP or VIP at a high-volume centre for poor-risk NSGCT, then restaging.
bullets: BEP x4 (or VIP x4 if bleomycin contraindicated); manage at a high-volume centre
Slow marker decline may prompt treatment intensification on protocol
Brain imaging and prophylaxis considerations for high-hCG / extensive lung disease
Reassess markers and imaging on the restaging step
Backbones referenced below

nodes.name: NSGCT restaging
nodes.title: NSGCT: response-adapted restaging after chemotherapy
nodes.description: Re-image and repeat markers after first-line chemotherapy; the response pattern chooses surgery, surveillance, or salvage.
bullets: Complete response (markers normal, no residual mass): move to surveillance
Residual mass with normalised markers: resect all sites (post-chemotherapy RPLND) - not observed
Rising / plateaued markers: active disease - go to salvage systemic therapy, not surgery

nodes.name: Post-chemo RPLND
nodes.title: NSGCT residual (markers normal): resect all residual masses
nodes.description: Post-chemotherapy RPLND and resection of all residual sites when markers have normalised; histology directs what follows.
bullets: Resect all residual masses >= ~1 cm (post-chemotherapy RPLND +/- other sites) at a high-volume centre
Surgery is not for rising markers - those go to salvage
Resected histology (necrosis vs teratoma vs viable tumour) directs the next step
RPLND is a surgical procedure - no systemic dose protocol

nodes.name: Post-RPLND histology
nodes.title: Post-RPLND histology: what the resected mass showed
nodes.description: The pathology of the resected residual mass decides whether observation or adjuvant chemotherapy follows.
bullets: Necrosis / fibrosis only: no further therapy
Mature teratoma: complete resection is curative; no chemotherapy
Viable germ-cell tumour: consider two cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy, especially with adverse features / incomplete resection

nodes.name: Post-RPLND necrosis
nodes.title: Post-RPLND necrosis/fibrosis: observation
nodes.description: Necrosis or fibrosis only - no further therapy; enter surveillance.
bullets: Necrosis/fibrosis carries an excellent prognosis; no adjuvant chemotherapy
Enter routine post-treatment surveillance
Late relapse remains possible - keep to the surveillance schedule

nodes.name: Post-RPLND teratoma
nodes.title: Post-RPLND mature teratoma: complete resection alone
nodes.description: Mature teratoma is chemo-resistant but cured by complete surgical resection; no further chemotherapy.
bullets: Teratoma does not respond to chemotherapy - completeness of resection is what matters
Ensure all residual sites are cleared; residual teratoma can grow or transform
No adjuvant chemotherapy; enter routine post-treatment surveillance

nodes.name: Post-RPLND viable GCT
nodes.title: Post-RPLND viable germ-cell tumour: adjuvant chemotherapy
nodes.description: Viable tumour in the resected mass with adverse features prompts two cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy, then surveillance.
bullets: Two cycles of adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy for adverse features (>10% viable cells, incomplete resection, high-risk primary)
Complete resection with only focal viable tumour may be observed after multidisciplinary review
Then enter routine post-treatment surveillance
EP backbone referenced below

nodes.name: NSGCT restaging salvage
nodes.title: NSGCT restaging (rising markers): salvage chemotherapy
nodes.description: Rising or plateaued markers after first-line chemo indicate active disease - route to the relapse / salvage pathway.
bullets: Rising markers mean surgery will not cure - proceed to salvage systemic therapy
Refer to a high-volume germ-cell centre and enter the relapse pathway
VIP backbone referenced below
Options include conventional-dose salvage or high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Monitoring after curative therapy; most relapses are early and salvageable. A confirmed relapse routes to the relapse pathway.
bullets: Markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) and clinical review, most intensively in the first 2-3 years
Cross-sectional imaging of chest/abdomen/pelvis at intervals; taper over ~5 years
A confirmed marker rise or new mass re-enters the relapse pathway
Monitor late effects: cardiovascular risk, hypogonadism, secondary malignancy, neuropathy/ototoxicity
nodes.linkLabel: If relapse is confirmed: go to the relapse / salvage pathway

nodes.name: Relapse category
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory germ-cell tumour
nodes.description: Salvage choice depends on prior platinum response and timing of relapse.
bullets: Re-confirm markers and re-image; refer to a high-volume centre

bullets.label: Platinum-sensitive
bullets.sub: relapse after an initial response to first-line cisplatin

bullets.label: Platinum-refractory
bullets.sub: progression during or shortly after platinum

bullets.label: Late relapse
bullets.sub: > ~2 years after chemo; often chemo-resistant, surgery-led

nodes.name: Conventional salvage
nodes.title: Platinum-sensitive relapse: conventional-dose salvage (VIP / TIP)
nodes.description: Standard-dose cisplatin-based salvage combinations for platinum-sensitive relapse, then salvage restaging.
bullets: Conventional-dose VIP or TIP (paclitaxel-ifosfamide-cisplatin)
High-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue is an alternative first salvage
Reassess markers and imaging afterward on the salvage-restaging step
VIP backbone referenced below

nodes.name: High-dose salvage
nodes.title: Platinum-refractory relapse: high-dose chemo + ASCT
nodes.description: High-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell transplant for refractory disease, then salvage restaging.
bullets: High-dose carboplatin/etoposide with autologous stem-cell rescue (often tandem cycles)
Best delivered at an experienced transplant/germ-cell centre
No dedicated dose protocol here - delivered on a transplant protocol
Reassess markers and imaging afterward on the salvage-restaging step

nodes.name: Late relapse
nodes.title: Late relapse (> 2 years): surgery-led
nodes.description: Late relapses are frequently chemo-resistant - complete surgical resection is prioritised.
bullets: Complete surgical resection is the treatment of choice where technically feasible
Chemotherapy is often less effective; reserve salvage systemic therapy for unresectable disease
Manage at a high-volume centre with germ-cell surgical expertise

nodes.name: Salvage restaging
nodes.title: Salvage: response-adapted restaging
nodes.description: After salvage chemotherapy, marker and imaging response decide resection of residual disease vs later-line therapy.
bullets: Markers normalised with a residual mass: resect all residual sites (desperation surgery in selected cases)
Rising / plateaued markers: platinum-refractory - move to later-line / trial therapy
Manage at a high-volume germ-cell centre

nodes.name: Post-salvage resection
nodes.title: Post-salvage residual (markers normal): resection
nodes.description: Resect all residual masses after salvage when markers have normalised.
bullets: Resect all residual masses after salvage as in first-line, at a high-volume centre
Histology (necrosis / teratoma / viable tumour) again guides prognosis and any further therapy
Even selected patients with slowly rising markers and resectable disease may benefit from desperation surgery
Then resume close surveillance

nodes.name: Later-line therapy
nodes.title: Platinum-refractory after salvage: later-line / trial therapy
nodes.description: Later-line systemic options and clinical trials for multiply-relapsed, platinum-refractory germ-cell tumour.
bullets: Gemcitabine + oxaliplatin (+/- paclitaxel), or other platinum-refractory regimens
Prioritise clinical-trial enrolment where available
Resect isolated resectable disease even in the refractory setting
Integrate palliative and supportive care
GemOx backbone referenced below
